target_customer: Small businesses and entrepreneurs in the Philippines that need invoicing, payments, payroll and bill payment; later platforms and companies needing payouts
problem: Filipino banks impose setup fees, minimum balances and heavy requirements on small businesses, which pushes them toward cash and informal tools for invoicing, collecting and paying.
business_model: Fintech payments and payouts, fees on transactions and disbursements; later an API for platforms using its BSP operator of payment system registration
product_category: SMB digital banking, then payment and disbursement infrastructure

founders.name: Don Pansacola
prior_employers: OpenDNS (early core product team, later acquired by Cisco)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists software engineering, blockchain and distributed systems background. Education not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Aldrich Tan
founders.background_notes: Design leader; Managing Director of the nonprofit UXPH per the YC page. Education not found.

competitors.name: Maya (PayMaya, Voyager Innovations)
competitors.what: Digital wallet and payments player that obtained a BSP digital bank approval and sold business accounts to SMEs
competitors.traction_then: Large consumer and merchant base; exact SME numbers not found
competitors.funding_then: Backed by Voyager Innovations / PLDT group

technical_complexity.rationale: A multi-product fintech stack on top of local bank rails and e-wallets (invoicing, collections, batch payouts) needing regulatory registration, but built from standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Operator of payment system registration with the BSP is a modest barrier; the product features were copyable by wallets and banks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Larger wallets and digital banks pushed into SME banking; NextPay later closed payment acceptance products and focused on disbursements.

market_need_then: Bank accounts for small businesses in the Philippines were hard to open and costly per the YC description, and a Maya commissioned study (secondary, self interested) claimed 94 percent of SME transactions were in cash.

branding.domain_note: Originally nextpay.world, which now redirects with a 301 to nextpay.ph; acquisition history not found.

identity.visual_style: Product-led fintech styling; the CXO is a design leader

branding.brand_signature: Product family named with a Next prefix (NextInvoice, NextCollect, NextPayout, NextAPI)

brand_strength.rationale: Local press coverage of the seed round but no evidence of brand driven growth; the name is generic and shared with other payment companies.

pivots.from: SMB digital banking with payment acceptance, invoices and payment links
pivots.to: Disbursement, payables and payroll infrastructure and API
pivots.why: Company said it closed payment acceptance products to focus on disbursements; exact date not stated in the sources I opened.

outcome_analysis: NextPay raised a 125 thousand dollar YC investment in 2021 and a 1.6 million dollar seed round in July 2021 from regional and local investors. No later round was found. It narrowed its scope from a broad SMB bank substitute to disbursements and a BSP regulated payouts API, which suggests the broader banking offer faced strong competition from wallets and digital banks. It remains active with about 25 staff per YC.
notes: Seed confirmed by several outlets (Manila Bulletin, Philstar, ABS-CBN, BusinessWorld, Fintech News PH). One report puts total raised at about 1.9 million dollars. Artie Lopez is described as a third co-founder in a Pansacola profile seen in search results only, so not listed as a founder. Founding year conflicts (2019 vs 2020). The Maya source date is approximate (2021). Inquirer seed article returned HTTP 403 and was not read.
